xrefcode.com / docs / cli / edges

$ xref edges

by Alexander Panasenko · xrefcode.com
On this page
  1. Usage
  2. Arguments and options
  3. Examples
  4. Edges from a perf recording
  5. Limits
  6. Provenance

Import observed caller → callee adjacencies from saved stacks (address lists, perf script call chains, folded stacks) into an evidence store that graph queries use when asked to. Static call graphs miss calls through pointers; observed stacks fill some of them in. Counts are stack samples, not call counts.

Usage

xref edges import [OPTIONS] --out <OUT>

Arguments and options

Options

--input <INPUT>
Saved addresses, perf script, or root-first folded stacks; '-' reads stdin.
default -
--format <FORMAT>
[possible values: addresses, perf, folded].
default addresses
--base <BASE>
Runtime address of the lowest image virtual address (not an arbitrary text mapping).
--maps <MAPS>
Saved /proc/PID/maps from the sampled process, not the current process.
--target-path <TARGET_PATH>
Original executable path as it appears in maps/MMAP records.
--pid <PID>
Process TGID to select from perf-script samples.
--build-id <BUILD_ID>
Reject a mismatch against the selected binary's build ID.
--kind <KIND>
Auto: sampled leaf is instruction IP, ancestors are return addresses [possible values: auto, instruction, return-address, static, symbol].
default auto
--max-bytes <MAX_BYTES>
Input byte budget; reading stops there and the result is marked truncated.
default 2147483648
--max-samples <MAX_SAMPLES>
Stack sample budget; reading stops there and the result is marked truncated.
default 100000
--timeout-ms <TIMEOUT_MS>
Time budget in milliseconds; reading stops there and the result is marked truncated.
default 30000
--out <OUT>
Path of the edge evidence store to write.

Examples

Edges from a perf recording

The ripgrep recording from profile import, converted with perf script -i rg.perf.data > rg.perf.txt:

Command
$ xref -b rg edges import --format perf --input rg.perf.txt --maps rg.maps --pid 4084848 --out rg.edges
Output
imported 12 observed stack-adjacency edges from 3991 samples; counts are stack samples
warning: fde_ranges_are_not_source_function_boundaries
warning: imported_trace_producer_not_authenticated
warning: perf_callchain_ancestors_treated_as_return_addresses
warning: some_target_mappings_not_independently_build_id_verified
warning: stack_adjacency_and_sample_counts_are_not_direct_calls_or_invocation_counts
warning: unknown_frames_preserved_edges_never_bridge_them
stderr
xref: load 2.7ms, total 43.1ms

Formats, the store, and how queries opt in: Offline stacks and observed call evidence.

Limits

  • Adjacent frames show that one function was on the stack under another, not how many calls were made.
  • The mapping is supplied by the caller (--maps or --base); a wrong one gives wrong edges.

Provenance

Recorded with xref 0.5.0 (the remapped release build of commit b00d4a14, made by scripts/package-release.sh before the tag) on Linux x86-64, on rg = ripgrep 14.1.1 (official stripped release). Live examples ran against one ripgrep process filtering an endless input stream; commands shown with sudo ran as root. Output is unchanged except that whitespace at the end of each line and empty lines at the end of the output are removed; long outputs are cut where marked.
